Fact.Name: A section 4975 prohibited transaction occurred with respect to an HSA (writable)
Fact.Description:
The deemed-distribution character question, prohibited-transaction leg. The source states the situation directly (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 3, under the "Deemed Distributions From HSAs" heading at line 187): "You engaged in any transaction prohibited by section 4975 with respect to any of your HSAs, at any time in 2025. Your account ceases to be an HSA as of January 1, 2025, and you must include the fair market value of all assets in the account as of January 1, 2025, on line 14a", and the section closes at line 209 with "Any deemed distribution will not be treated as used to pay qualified medical expenses. Generally, these distributions are subject to the additional 20% tax."
RETURN-LEVEL, AND THAT IS THE POINT. When the top-level line 14a scalar was retired onto the /hsaDistributions collection, this attestation was NOT re-pointed at collection items, because a section 4975 prohibited transaction produces no Form 1099-SA — there is no document to enter and therefore no item to carry the answer. Re-pointing would have deleted the refusal rather than moved it. The module header records the decision in full.
THIS IS A FILER ATTESTATION, NOT A COMPUTATION. The graph holds no transaction history for any HSA, so whether a section 4975 prohibited transaction occurred is not derivable from anything it knows. The filer states it. This is the writable optional fact; use the derived alias /hasNonNormalTopLevelHsaDistribution downstream.
THE COLLECTION TWIN, for the filer who DOES hold a Form 1099-SA, is /hsaDistributions/*/hsaDistributionCode, whose enum already includes prohibitedTransaction. This is the same question asked of the filer who has no such document.

Fact.Name: A return-level section 4975 deemed distribution was attested
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe alias over /writableHsaProhibitedTransactionOccurred: FALSE when the filer has not answered, which is every return in the committed corpus, so the knockout that reads this fact is byte-identical to the pre-fill graph everywhere.
THE WRAPPER IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT STYLISTIC. hsa /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionCode is a dependency of flow /flowIsKnockedOut, so a bare unanswered Writable here would take /flowIsKnockedOut Incomplete by completeness contagion on EVERY return in the corpus. That is the /aotcMagi failure class, already documented elsewhere.
THE NAME KEEPS "TopLevel" ON PURPOSE after the retirement: it now reads as "return-level, not per-1099-SA", which is what this fact is. Renaming it would remove and re-add one key on all 969 committed cases for no behavioural gain.
CONSUMER: hsa /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionCode (SHIPPING, BlockSubmissionOnTrue), where it is a true-arm beside the collection-side /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionsNotNormal. The pledge leg routes to the OTHER knockout through the sibling alias /hasTopLevelHsaPledgedAsSecurity below; the two are deliberately not one fact.

Fact.Name: An HSA was used as security for a loan (writable)
Fact.Description:
The deemed-distribution character question, pledge leg. The source states the situation directly (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 3, under the "Deemed Distributions From HSAs" heading at line 187): "You used any portion of any of your HSAs as security for a loan at any time in 2025. You must include the fair market value of the assets used as security for the loan as income on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8f."
RETURN-LEVEL, AND THAT IS THE POINT, for the same reason as its prohibited-transaction sibling above: a pledge produces no Form 1099-SA, so there is no /hsaDistributions item to re-point this onto. See the module header for the retirement in full.
THIS IS A FILER ATTESTATION, NOT A COMPUTATION: the graph holds no HSA transaction or pledge history. Use the derived alias /hasTopLevelHsaPledgedAsSecurity downstream.
NOTE WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT DO, so a later reader does not mistake its scope. The source routes the pledged FMV to Schedule 1 line 8f as income, and this fill does NOT compute that amount or add it to income — the return is REFUSED before the amount matters, exactly as the collection-side /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV already refuses the Box-4 case rather than computing it. Modeling the line 8f amount is the deferred follow-on, and it needs an FMV intake this node deliberately does not add.

Fact.Name: A return-level HSA pledge as loan security was attested
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe alias over /writableHsaPledgedAsSecurityForLoan: FALSE when the filer has not answered, which is every return in the committed corpus.
THE WRAPPER IS LOAD-BEARING for the same reason as the sibling alias above: hsa /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV is a dependency of flow /flowIsKnockedOut, so a bare unanswered Writable would take /flowIsKnockedOut Incomplete by contagion corpus-wide. The name keeps "TopLevel" for the reason the sibling states.
CONSUMER: hsa /flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV (SHIPPING, BlockSubmissionOnTrue), where it is a true-arm beside the existing Count over /hsaDistributions/*/causesFmvKnockout. The FMV knockout is the right twin for this leg because both turn on a fair market value the graph does not hold.

Fact.Name: Fair market value of the HSA assets pledged as security for a loan (writable)
Fact.Description:
The AMOUNT of the IRC 223(e)(2) / 408(e)(4) pledge deemed distribution, the companion of the character question /writableHsaPledgedAsSecurityForLoan above. This fact supplies the pledged-as-security case of the death treatment, which needs exactly this fair-market-value intake. Read through /schedule1Line8fPledgedHsaFmvIncome, never directly.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION (operator rule: the application builds the screen from this Description and never opens an IRS document).
THE QUESTION: "What were the HSA assets you used as security for the loan worth?"
HELP TEXT: "When you use any part of an HSA as security for a loan, the law treats that part as paid out to you, so it counts as income for 2025. Enter what the pledged portion was worth - not the whole account, unless you pledged the whole account, and not the amount of the loan." (Paraphrasing the 2025 Instructions for Form 8889, "Deemed Distributions From HSAs": "You used any portion of any of your HSAs as security for a loan at any time in 2025. You must include the fair market value of the assets used as security for the loan as income on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8f"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 3, the heading at line 187. Pub. 969 says the same in its own words, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p969.pdf, page 9. The statute is IRC 223(e)(2) applying IRC 408(e)(4), "the portion so used is treated as distributed to that individual"; 26 U.S.C. 408, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section408&num=0&edition=2024.)
ASKED WHEN: /hasTopLevelHsaPledgedAsSecurity is true - that is, immediately after the filer answers the pledge attestation yes. Asked ONCE FOR THE RETURN, not per filer, because the attestation it follows is return-level (the module header above records why: a pledge produces no Form 1099-SA, so there is no document to attribute) and because its destination, Schedule 1 line 8f, is a return-level line that Form 8889's per-individual structure never touches. Never asked otherwise.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED - and so, for now, is the ANSWERED case. hsa:/flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV blocks submission on EVERY attested pledge while the 20% additional-tax question in the banner above is open with the project owner. The application should still ask the question: the amount is computed, it lands on Schedule 1 line 8f, and the ruling that retires the refusal needs no new intake. The PERMANENT part of the residue, the part that survives the ruling either way, is an attested pledge with no amount behind it: the alternative is to file a return that admits a deemed distribution happened and reports $0 of it.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Limit type="Min" $0. No upper bound - the pledged portion can be the whole account and an HSA balance has no statutory ceiling. $0 is a valid answer (a pledge of assets worth nothing) and is told apart from "unanswered" by IsComplete on this Writable, not by a zero test.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /schedule1Line8fPledgedHsaFmvIncome, which is an addend of BOTH income /schedule1TotalOtherIncome (Schedule 1 line 9, the total) and hsa:/schedule1Line8fForm8889Income (the PRINTED line 8f box, PDF-bound at dictionary/pdf/2025/reviews/forms/IRS1040S1.json field f1_18[0]). Both are required: line 9 adds the legs individually and never reads the printed-box fact, so an amount named in only one of the two makes the filed Schedule 1 fail to foot. It does NOT feed Form 8889 line 14a (that line is for the section 4975 case, whose intake is hsa:/filers/*/writableHsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv). Whether it bears the 20% additional tax is the OPEN OPERATOR QUESTION in the banner above; the screen should say the amount is taxed as income and should NOT promise or deny the 20% until that is ruled.

Fact.Name: The pledged-assets fair market value was supplied
Fact.Description: The "source answered" predicate for /writableHsaPledgedAssetsFairMarketValue, and the only thing the narrowed guard hsa:/flowKnockoutHsaDistributionFMV reads. IsComplete over a BARE optional Writable with no default and no complete-safe wrapper of its own, so it is false until the filer types a number and true the moment they do, a typed $0 included. It is NOT IsComplete over a complete-safe fact, which would be the always-true trap.

Fact.Name: Pledged HSA assets included in income on Schedule 1 line 8f
Fact.Description:
The Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 8f leg of the pledge deemed distribution, and the addend income /schedule1TotalOtherIncome reads. The instructions name that line and no other for this amount: "You must include the fair market value of the assets used as security for the loan as income on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8f" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8889.pdf, page 3).
IT IS READ TWICE, ON PURPOSE, AND THAT IS THE FIX FOR A DEFECT AN EARLIER REWORK ALMOST SHIPPED (an adversarial-review finding). Its consumers are income /schedule1TotalOtherIncome, which is Schedule 1 line 9 (the TOTAL, built from the individual legs), and hsa:/schedule1Line8fForm8889Income, which IS printed box 8f and is what the PDF binds. As first written this leg reached only the line-9 total, so a pledge return printed $9,500 in the line-9 total and $0 in box 8f and the schedule did not foot. Naming an amount in both places is not double-counting: line 9 never reads the printed-box fact.
IT ADDS BESIDE THE OTHER 8f LEGS AND CANNOT DOUBLE-COUNT WITH ANY OF THEM. Line 8f is printed "Income from Form 8889" - one line for the whole form - and this return can carry several of its legs at once: hsa:/hsaCollectionRouteTaxableDistributions is the printed line 16 (taxable distributions actually paid out of Forms 1099-SA, plus, since this same unit, the section 4975 January-1 value that the instructions route THROUGH line 14a); hsa:/hsaTestingPeriodFailureIncomeAndAdditionalTax is the printed Part III line 20; and this leg is an amount the instructions send to line 8f WITHOUT passing through any printed Form 8889 line at all. A pledged portion of an account is not a distribution reported on any Form 1099-SA (a pledge produces no such document, which is why the attestation is return-level), and it is not the section 4975 whole-account value either - that is a different subparagraph of IRC 408(e) with a different measure, a different date and a different destination line.
GATED ON THE ATTESTATION AS WELL AS THE ANSWER, for the reason its section 4975 twin hsa:/filers/*/hsaDeemedDistributionJanuary1Fmv records at length: an amount left behind by an edited interview would otherwise put income on the return with nothing refusing it, which is taxpayer-ADVERSE. With /hasTopLevelHsaPledgedAsSecurity false the leg is a hard $0 and reads no HSA input at all.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0, load-bearing because the consumer is a shipping income total, and $0 on every committed scenario: no committed scenario answers the pledge attestation, so this sum is byte-identical.

The filer's HDHP annual deductible as the plan states it — the section 223(c)(2)(A)(i) quantity. Taxpayer-attested; there is no IRS form line for it, because the return never reports it. Optional: unanswered means the filer was not asked, and the comparison below then flags nothing.

The filer's HDHP annual out-of-pocket maximum as the plan states it, DEDUCTIBLE INCLUDED — the section 223(c)(2)(A)(ii) sum of the annual deductible and the other annual out-of-pocket expenses required under the plan, premiums excluded. Taxpayer-attested; no return line reports it. Optional: unanswered means the filer was not asked. The printed limit's footnote (out-of-network deductibles and expenses are outside it when the plan uses a provider network) is NOT modelled — see the block above.

True when this filer answered BOTH plan figures, holds a self-only or family HDHP, and the plan misses either section 223(c)(2)(A) prong. Positive polarity so the return-level roll-up can count failures the way this dictionary's other per-filer gates do. Complete-safe FALSE through the terminal Case: a filer who was not asked, or whose coverage type is Incomplete, or who answered "both" (already knocked out), is never flagged. Both bounds are INCLUSIVE — a deductible exactly at the minimum and an out-of-pocket maximum exactly at the maximum both qualify.

Every filer's HDHP meets the section 223(c)(2)(A) deductible and out-of-pocket limits — the ADVISORY output of triage finding FED-1040-8889-HDHPTHRESH-001, and the fact that finally consumes the four TY2025 HDHP constants. TRUE unless some filer's answered plan figures miss a prong, so on every return that does not answer the new questions it is Complete true and nothing is flagged, exactly today's behaviour. NON-BLOCKING BY CONSTRUCTION: no computed line reads it and it is deliberately NOT a knockout — the finding asks to flag the mismatch, not to refuse the return. Its consumer is downstream of this repo, which is what the Export declares; the moment anything here reads it to alter a deduction or block a submission, it has become a different change with a different review.

True when the completed plan-figure comparison indicates that one or more filers' reported HDHP figures miss a section 223(c)(2)(A) deductible or out-of-pocket limit. Show this as an advisory asking the filer to review the plan figures and HSA eligibility. It is not an eligibility determination, does not change a deduction or exclusion, and must not block filing. The out-of-network footnote can make the comparison flag a plan that is still an HDHP, so the filer-facing warning must disclose that caveat. False when the plan figures were not supplied.
